newsitem.title: USA: Apple reorganises customer sales, service.
newsitem.headline: Apple reorganises customer sales, service.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc said on Tuesday it will consolidate its product development, marketing, sales, support and operations efforts.
The company said its new Worldwide Sales and Support Organisation will oversee selling and providing services to its education, business and consumer customers and will be divided geographically.
Apple outlined the divisions as follows:

* The North America Business Division, which will focus on three markets: PEN (Publishing/Entertainment/New Media), Enterprise, and SED (Scientific/Engineering/Design), including NeXT Sales and Professional Services. Mitch Manditch will be acting as head of North America Business Division.
* North America Education Division, which focuses on two markets, K-12 and Higher Education, and will be led by Mike Lorion.
* North America Consumer Division will focus on two markets, Consumer and the Macintosh Installed Base, and will be led by H.L. Cheung
* EMEA (Europe, Middle East, Africa) will drive its region's sales and support, led by Jan Larsen.
* Japan will cover the same responsibilities for the Japanese market, led by Tetsuya Shiga.
* Asia-Pacific will cover the same responsibilities for the Asia-Pacific market, and will be led by Steve Vamos.
* Latin America will cover the same responsibilities for the Latin American market, and will be led by Luis Rubio.
* AppleAssist Division remains responsible for Apple's Customer Service and Warranty activities, led by Mike Dionne.
* Claris will continue to sell Claris and Apple Software worldwide, led by Dominique Goupil.

"A number of activities which were previously joined with the sales organisation -- engineering, manufacturing, operations, marketing and product business management -- have moved into global, functional groups. Apple's sales organisation now focuses on one thing and one thing only -- sales and support to serve our customers and fulfill their demand worldwide," Apple Chairman Gilbert Amelio said in a release.
The company did not provide any figures on the cost or savings of the measures, but earlier on Tuesday Amelio announced a restructuring intended to save $400 million a year.
